title: Can We Predict Chemical Reactions from Quantum Mechanics?
problem: Investigate a fundamental open problem in theoretical and computational chemistry: given molecular composition, initial structure, and physical environment, can we predict which chemical reactions occur, their pathways, rate constants, selectivities, and product distributions from quantum mechanics with independently validated accuracy? Even though molecular dynamics is governed by quantum mechanics, general predictive solutions remain out of reach for complex, reactive, many-body systems. Examine the limits of electronic-structure approximations, nuclear quantum effects, transition-state and rare-event sampling, solvent and temperature coupling, and combinatorial reaction-network exploration. Choose tractable benchmark reactions and formulate falsifiable prospective predictions; distinguish exact principles from computational approximations and observed outcomes. Do not imply that solving a benchmark reaction solves the general problem. Deliver prioritized research hypotheses, uncertainty budgets, discriminating calculations or experiments, and explicit limitations.

strategies.title: Electronic-structure accuracy and uncertainty
strategies.approach: Compare methods for potential-energy surfaces and reaction barriers on a small benchmark reaction with high-quality reference data. Quantify correlation, basis-set, multireference, and model errors and how these propagate into predicted rates.
strategies.summary: A reproducible error budget and method-selection rule.

strategies.title: Reaction pathway discovery
strategies.approach: Evaluate whether unbiased or enhanced-search methods recover all kinetically relevant pathways for a defined reactive system. Use independently known pathways where possible; state coverage and stopping criteria.
strategies.summary: A pathway-coverage benchmark and clear missed-pathway failure modes.

strategies.title: Dynamics and rare events
strategies.approach: Test transition-state theory and rare-event sampling against dynamical recrossing, nonstatistical behavior, and nuclear quantum effects on a selected reaction.
strategies.summary: A quantitative prediction with uncertainty and a falsifying observable.

strategies.title: Solvent and environmental coupling
strategies.approach: Compare gas-phase, implicit-solvent, and explicit-environment predictions for a benchmark reaction; assess temperature, pressure, and ionic effects where relevant.
strategies.summary: A discriminating experiment or computation that isolates environment-induced changes.

strategies.title: From mechanisms to product distributions
strategies.approach: Construct a bounded reaction network and propagate elementary-step uncertainties into measurable yields, rates, and selectivity under unseen conditions. Evaluate prospective out-of-sample prediction.
strategies.summary: A preregisterable prediction and validation plan for products and rates.
